TWO MORE INSTANCES OF THE RESEND FRICTION, 2026-08-31, AND THE SECOND ONE SHOWS A CONSEQUENCE NOBODY HAD RECORDED.

`fact:changing-one-sentence-in-a-long-decision-cost-a-full-6242-character-resend` (2026-08-19) measured the cost precisely — two resends of 6,242 and 6,455 characters to change one sentence each — and noted "four projects have now reported the pattern". Nothing in it is overturned.

═══ ① A FIFTH PROJECT, INDEPENDENTLY ═══
`proj:bhome`, a consumer design with no connection to reflow2's subject matter: "revising one field of a long node means re-sending that whole field. For a Decision whose `decision` text is several paragraphs, appending a line is disproportionately expensive and is the one operation where the revision-safety warning is most likely to be earned. An append mode, or field-level patch, would help."

═══ 🛑 ② AND A SIXTH, FIRST-HAND, WHERE THE COST CHANGED WHERE THE INFORMATION LANDED ═══
This session needed to record that `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` describes a flat ten subsystems while the graph holds 8 subsystems plus 2 systems of five — a correction belonging in the decision's own text, beside the four count-amendments already written there.

IT WAS NOT PUT THERE. The `decision` field is multi-kilobyte, appending one paragraph meant re-sending all of it, and the tool's own warning says the prior value would exist only in the reply. The correction went into the node's EMPTY `rationale` field instead, and the same avoidance was taken again minutes later on `dec:idea-should-optimize-be-a-served-skill-any-project-can-run`. Both times the reply confirmed it: "This call added properties to an existing node and overwrote nothing."

⭐⭐ SO THE COST IS NOT ONLY TOKENS AND NOT ONLY RISK — IT IS PLACEMENT. A reader who opens `bl83a` and reads the `decision` field, which is where its own four previous amendments live, will not meet the fifth. The correction is one field away, in a field whose declared purpose is WHY the choice was made rather than WHAT was decided. The information is in the graph and it is in the wrong place, and it is in the wrong place because the right place was expensive to edit.

⇒ THE NODES MOST WORTH CORRECTING ARE THE LONGEST, WHICH ARE EXACTLY THE ONES WHERE THE WORKAROUND IS MOST TEMPTING. The 08-19 fact already observed the safety version of this — "the nodes most worth editing are the ones most dangerous to edit". This is the same asymmetry producing a second, quieter failure: not a lost edit, a misfiled one.

⚠️ BOUNDS. ② is self-observed by the session that did it, so the judgement that the content belonged in `decision` rather than `rationale` is arguable — a correction to a decision's premise is not obviously the wrong thing to put in its rationale, and a reader who reads both fields loses nothing. The claim is narrower than "this was wrong": it is that the FIELD WAS CHOSEN BY EDIT COST RATHER THAN BY MEANING, which is true regardless of which field a careful author would have picked with no cost difference.
